subject.title: Request: Add Discord reaction event support to Hooks system

question: Should OpenClaw add dedicated observation-only reaction Hooks for Discord now, fold this into a broader non-message event API, or document the existing system-event path as the supported plugin automation surface?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but the permanent API shape affects third-party plugin compatibility and overlaps with broader inbound event and wake-policy work.

options.title: Add generic reaction hooks
options.body: Define `reaction_added` and `reaction_removed` as observation-only plugin Hooks with a structured cross-channel payload, then wire Discord first with docs and tests.

options.title: Fold into non-message events
options.body: Make this request part of the broader public non-message inbound event contract so reactions, edits, typing, and read receipts share one SDK surface.

options.title: Document system events only
options.body: Declare routed system events as the supported plugin path for reactions and close hook-specific requests if maintainers do not want a new Hook API.

recommendation.title: Add generic reaction hooks
recommendation.body: Define `reaction_added` and `reaction_removed` as observation-only plugin Hooks with a structured cross-channel payload, then wire Discord first with docs and tests.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision spans Discord reaction handling, plugin SDK boundaries, and product direction, and steipete is the strongest recent history match across those surfaces.
